label: Open travel planner
summary: Going by its name, opens the travel planner from the activity window; it takes one argument and returns nothing.
details: The game's own texts and GUI files never use it, and its argument is undocumented.

label: Activity window itself
summary: The activity window object itself, handed on as a value; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Other windows have a function of the same name, and vanilla texts use it to pass the current item to other functions.

label: Sort guest subset, all phases
summary: Going by its name, sets how a named subset of guests is sorted in every phase of the activity, taking two arguments.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it. The sibling function with the Descending ending is used with a subset name and a sort value name, so the two arguments are probably those, but this is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the name of the guest subset.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Probably the name of the value to sort by.

label: Sort guests descending, all phases
summary: Going by its name and use, sets that a named subset of guests is sorted from highest to lowest by a named sort value, in every phase of the activity.
details: Vanilla calls it when a widget starts, for example with the subset 'charioteers' and the sort value 'charioteer_victory_score_value' in the chariot race widget, and with 'supporter' and 'coronation_supporter_sort_value' in the coronation widget. The meaning of the two arguments is read from those uses, not from a doc.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the guest subset.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The name of the sort value that decides the order.
fields.values: a text naming a sort value

label: Set guest sorting
summary: Going by its name, sets how one named subset of guests is sorted, taking three arguments.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it, and its arguments are undocumented.

label: Set guest sorting descending
summary: Going by its name, sets that one named subset of guests is sorted from highest to lowest, taking three arguments.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it, and its arguments are undocumented.

label: Sort guests
summary: Going by its name, sorts a subset of the activity's guests, taking three arguments.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it, and its arguments are undocumented.

label: Sort guests descending
summary: Going by its name, sorts a subset of the activity's guests from highest to lowest, taking three arguments.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it, and its arguments are undocumented.

label: Update guest subset
summary: Going by its name, refreshes the guest subset of an activity phase; it takes one argument and returns nothing.
details: Vanilla uses a function of this name on the activity locale window with the current planned phase (`PlannedActivityPhase.Self`), when a widget starts and on click. That is a hint from another type, not proof for this one.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the activity phase to refresh, going by the same name on another type.

label: Background data, access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the background data object itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered. Other types have a function of this name that is used to pass the current widget on.

label: Background environment
summary: Going by its name, the 3D environment (scene setting) of the activity window's background; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered. Vanilla uses a function of this name on another type to pick the scene for animated portraits.

label: Background texture
summary: Going by its name, the texture (image) used as the activity window's background; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered. The same name on other types is used for coat of arms images.

label: Background data itself
summary: The background data object itself, handed on as a value; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts use a function of this name on other types to pass the current item on.

label: Window character, access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the activity window character entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered.

label: Character animation
summary: Going by its name, the name of the animation the character plays in the activity window, as text.
details: Vanilla uses functions of this name on other types to choose the animation of a portrait. Nothing uses it on this type.

label: Character camera
summary: Going by its name, the camera used to show the character in the activity window; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered. Nothing uses it on this type.

label: Character
summary: The character that this entry of the activity window stands for.
details: Vanilla's activity windows use it as the data context of a widget, so everything inside shows that character. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Character label
summary: A text that labels this character in the activity window.
details: Vanilla shows it directly as the text of a widget in the activity windows.

label: Window character itself
summary: The activity window character entry itself, handed on as a value; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts use a function of this name on other types to pass the current item on.

label: Add friend window, access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the add friend window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered.

label: Hide add friend window
summary: Going by its name, closes the add friend window.
details: Its one use is a button in the engine's add friend window that calls it when clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Add friend window itself
summary: The add friend window itself, handed on as a value; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts use a function of this name on other types to pass the current item on.

label: Show add friend window
summary: Going by its name, whether the add friend window should be shown.
details: Its one use decides whether the engine's add friend window is visible.

label: Show add friend window
summary: Going by its name, shows the add friend window; it returns nothing.
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it on this type. The sample lines the input shows for this name are unrelated texts.

label: Add tradition window, access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the add tradition window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered.

label: Add the tradition
summary: Adds the tradition that is selected in the add tradition window to the culture.
details: Vanilla runs it on the click of the confirm button of the window. It returns nothing.

label: Can add tradition
summary: Whether the selected tradition can be added now (yes or no).
details: Vanilla uses it to enable or disable the confirm button of the add tradition window.

label: Can buy tradition
summary: Whether the given tradition can be bought now (yes or no).
details: Vanilla passes the tradition of the current list entry and shows a widget when the answer is no, so it marks entries that cannot be bought. The exact conditions are not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a culture tradition, for example the current list entry

label: Can pay cost
summary: Whether the cost of the tradition change can be paid (yes or no).
details: Vanilla shows a widget next to the cost text when the answer is no.

label: Can pick and buy tradition
summary: Going by its name, whether the given tradition can both be picked and bought (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it. Compare CanPickTradition and CanBuyTradition, which check the two parts.

label: Can pick tradition
summary: Whether the given tradition can be picked in the window now (yes or no).
details: Vanilla passes the tradition of the current list entry. It enables the entry when the answer is yes and shows a blocker widget when it is no.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a culture tradition, for example the current list entry

label: Close window
summary: Closes the add tradition window.
details: Vanilla runs it on the click of the close and cancel buttons of the window. It returns nothing.

label: Blockers text
summary: A text that lists what stops the selected tradition from being added.
details: Vanilla puts it in the tooltip of the establish tradition and replace tradition buttons.

label: Cost breakdown
summary: A text that shows how the cost of the tradition change is made up.
details: Vanilla puts it under the total cost in the cost tooltips for adding and for replacing a tradition.

label: Cost text
summary: The total cost of the tradition change, as a ready-made text.
details: Vanilla shows it after "Cost:" in the window and in the cost tooltips, for adding and for replacing a tradition.

label: Pick blockers text
summary: A text that lists what stops the given tradition from being picked.
details: Vanilla passes the tradition of the current list entry and shows the text on the entry and in its tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a culture tradition, for example the current list entry

label: Replaced tradition
summary: The tradition that would be replaced by the selected one.
details: Vanilla uses it in the replace tradition tooltip, where it takes the name of that tradition. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Selected tradition
summary: The tradition currently selected in the add tradition window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the detail part of the window. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Selected tradition group
summary: Going by its name, the group (category block) of the selected tradition; the game documents nothing more.
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it. The return type is not registered.

label: Tradition cost
summary: The cost of the given tradition, as a ready-made text.
details: Vanilla passes the tradition of the current list entry and shows the result as text on that entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tradition whose cost to show.
fields.values: a culture tradition, for example the current list entry

label: Tradition cost breakdown
summary: A text that shows how the cost of the given tradition is made up.
details: Vanilla passes the tradition of the current list entry and uses the result as the tooltip of its cost.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tradition whose cost to explain.
fields.values: a culture tradition, for example the current list entry

label: Tradition group
summary: The tradition group (a block of traditions in the window) with the given name.
details: Vanilla asks for the groups 'realm' and 'combat' and uses them as data context; its category is used to pick the tab shown when the window starts. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from those uses.

label: Has tradition category
summary: Whether the window has the given tradition category (yes or no).
details: Vanilla passes the category of a tradition group and uses the answer to show the category's tab and to mark it as pressed.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: the category of a tradition group

label: Is replacing
summary: Going by its name, whether the window is replacing an existing tradition rather than adding a new one (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Add tradition window itself
summary: The add tradition window itself, handed on as a value; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts use a function of this name on other types to pass the current item on.

label: Select tradition
summary: Makes the given tradition the selected one in the add tradition window.
details: Vanilla runs it on the click of a tradition in the list, passing that tradition. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a culture tradition, for example the clicked list entry

label: Set tradition category
summary: Switches the window to the given tradition category.
details: Vanilla runs it when the window starts, with the category of the 'realm' group, and when a category tab is clicked. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: the category of a tradition group

label: Admin item, access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the administration item itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered.

label: Levies
summary: Going by its name, the number of levy troops that this administration item provides.
details: Not used on this type. Vanilla shows the same name on the related theme and title items as a number with a soldier icon in the government administration window.

label: Taxes
summary: Going by its name, the tax gold that this administration item provides.
details: Not used on this type. Vanilla shows the same name on the related theme and title items as a number with a gold icon in the government administration window.

label: Title
summary: Going by its name, the title that this administration item belongs to; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered. Not used on this type.

label: Title prominence
summary: Going by its name, a number for how prominent the item's title is.
details: Not used on this type. Vanilla shows the same name on the prominent theme item as a number with two decimals in the government administration window.

label: Has player candidate
summary: Going by its name, whether the local player has a candidate for this administration item (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Has player candidate in first
summary: Going by its name, whether the local player has a candidate among the first places of this item (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it. What counts as the first places is not documented.

label: Player independent in first
summary: Going by its name, whether the local player is an independent ruler who is among the first places of this item (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it. The exact meaning is not documented.

label: Player has invested
summary: Going by its name, whether the local player has invested in this administration item (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Player invested in top
summary: Going by its name, whether the local player has invested in the top candidate of this item (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Has valid successor
summary: Going by its name, whether this administration item has a valid successor (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Is assigned
summary: Going by its name, whether this administration item is assigned to someone (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Admin item itself
summary: The administration item itself, handed on as a value; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts use a function of this name on other types to pass the current item on.

label: Family group, access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the family group item itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered.

label: Family items
summary: The list of family entries inside this family group, for a list widget to show.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the government administration window. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Family group name
summary: The name of this family group, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a widget in the government administration window.

label: Family group itself
summary: The family group item itself, handed on as a value; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts use a function of this name on other types to pass the current item on.

label: Family item, access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the family item itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered.

label: House
summary: The dynasty house that this family entry stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a widget in the government administration window, so the widget shows that house. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Rank and power
summary: Going by its name, a text with the family's rank and power.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a widget in the government administration window. What exactly it contains is not documented.

label: Is bloc leader
summary: Going by its name, whether this family is the leader of its bloc (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Family item itself
summary: The family item itself, handed on as a value; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts use a function of this name on other types to pass the current item on.

label: Merit pool, access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the merit pool itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered.

label: Contains candidate
summary: Going by its name, whether the given character is a candidate in this merit pool (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character to look for, probably.

label: Candidate position
summary: The place of the given character in the line of candidates of this merit pool, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as "N in line" in the title appointment window and shows "None" when it is 0. A merit pool is a group of characters who can be appointed to titles of one tier.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose place to give.
fields.values: a character, for example the current list entry

label: Candidate tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the given candidate in this merit pool.
details: Vanilla passes the character of the current list entry and uses the result as that entry's tooltip in the government administration window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character, for example the current list entry

label: Pool type name
summary: The name of this merit pool's type (for example civilian or military), as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the heading of the pool tooltip in the title appointment window. The two example types come from the pool's military check used nearby.

label: Pool type tag
summary: A short text tag that identifies this merit pool's type.
details: Vanilla checks whether an obligation level has this tag, to decide if a widget is visible.

label: Required merit level
summary: The merit level a character needs to join this merit pool, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of widgets in the government administration window; a related text says characters need a merit level of at least this value.

label: Better same-rank candidates
summary: Going by its name, how many candidates of the same rank have a higher career score than the given one, as a whole number.
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Tier frame
summary: Going by its name, a whole number that picks the frame (image variant) matching the tier of this merit pool.
details: Vanilla uses it as the frame of an icon in the government administration window.

label: Pool heading
summary: A text used as the heading of the merit pool window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the header text of the window that opens for a merit pool in the government administration window.

label: Title tier name
summary: The name of the title tier of this merit pool, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the pool names, as in "Civilian [tier] merit pool", and in the merit requirement text.

label: Pool tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text of this merit pool.
details: Nothing uses it on this type. The same name on other types gives the tooltip of that object.

label: Has career score potential
summary: Going by its name and use, whether the given character could still gain career score in this merit pool (yes or no).
details: Vanilla combines it with a check that the character has no new appointment cooldown to decide if a widget is visible. The exact rule is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character, for example the current list entry

label: Is military pool
summary: Whether this merit pool is a military one rather than a civilian one (yes or no).
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide widgets and to pick the military or standard icon in tooltips. The civilian reading follows from the "not military" use in the same window.

label: Merit pool itself
summary: The merit pool itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla passes it to the administration window's function that sets the character list to show, when a pool is clicked. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Map icon, access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the province map icon itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered.

label: Governor
summary: The governor of the province this map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a widget in the map icon layer. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Province obligation level
summary: The obligation level of the province this map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a widget in the map icon layer. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Province taxes
summary: The tax gold this province contributes, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it with two decimals and a gold icon in the tooltip of the vassal map mode.

label: Province title
summary: The title of the province this map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a widget in the map icon layer. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Province troops
summary: The levy troops this province contributes, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a whole number with a soldier icon in the tooltip of the vassal map mode.

label: Map icon itself
summary: The province map icon itself, handed on as a value; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts use a function of this name on other types to pass the current item on.

label: Governor
summary: The governor shown in the vassal detail view.

label: Hired troops
summary: The hired troops of the vassal shown in the detail view.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a widget in that window. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Levy contribution
summary: How many levy troops this vassal contributes, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a whole number in the vassal details.

label: Levy efficiency bonus
summary: The bonus to levy efficiency for this vassal, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in brackets with a sign, next to the levy contribution. Whether it is a percentage is not stated.

label: Number of counties
summary: How many de jure counties (counties that belong to a title by the map's fixed borders) the vassal view counts, as a whole number.

label: Preferred candidate
summary: The candidate that is preferred as successor in the vassal detail view.

label: Main contract item
summary: The primary contract and obligation entry of the vassal shown in the detail view.

label: Succession line text

label: Succession score breakdown

label: Tax efficiency bonus
summary: The bonus to tax efficiency for this vassal, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in brackets with a sign, next to the tax contribution. Whether it is a percentage is not stated.

label: Vassal title
summary: The title of the vassal shown in the detail view.

label: Regiments
summary: The list of regiments of this administrative title.
details: Vanilla checks whether it has items, together with whether the title holder is an administrative ruler, to decide if a widget is visible. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Taxes
summary: How much tax gold this administrative title provides, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it with two decimals and a gold icon in the government administration window.

label: Tier
summary: Going by its name, the tier (rank) of this administrative title; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered. Nothing uses it on this type; vanilla uses a function of this name on another type as text in the domicile window.

label: Title
summary: The title that this entry stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a widget in the government administration window. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.

label: Title prominence
summary: Going by its name, a number for how prominent this title is.
details: Not used on this type. Vanilla shows the same name on the prominent theme item as a number with two decimals in the government administration window.

label: Total men-at-arms
summary: The total number of men-at-arms (professional soldiers) of this title, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as the troop count of the theme title in the government administration window.

label: Has player candidate
summary: Going by its name, whether the local player has a candidate for this title (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Has player candidate in first
summary: Going by its name, whether the local player has a candidate among the first places for this title (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it. What counts as the first places is not documented.

label: Player independent in first
summary: Going by its name, whether the local player is an independent ruler who is among the first places for this title (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it. The exact meaning is not documented.

label: Player has invested
summary: Going by its name, whether the local player has invested in this title (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Player invested in top
summary: Going by its name, whether the local player has invested in the top candidate for this title (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Has valid successor
summary: Going by its name, whether this title has a valid successor (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Is assigned
summary: Going by its name, whether this title is assigned to someone (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Title item itself
summary: The administrative title item itself, handed on as a value; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts use a function of this name on other types to pass the current item on.

label: Should show title
summary: Whether this title should be shown (yes or no).
details: Vanilla uses it to decide the visibility of a widget in the government administration window. The exact rule is not documented.

label: Should show tooltip
summary: Going by its name, whether a tooltip should be shown for this title (yes or no).
details: Nothing in the game's texts or GUI files uses it.

label: Agent slot, access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the agent slot itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered.

label: Slot name
summary: The name of this agent slot of a scheme, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text that says a character fills this agent slot in a scheme.

label: Slot scheme
summary: The scheme that this agent slot belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it to take the scheme's name in the text that says a character fills the slot. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation, so the type is read from that use.
